_comment: Deliberately NOT named 'fixture.json' -- tests/contracts/test_gate_policy_is_shared.py globs tests/fixtures/**/fixture.json and its _QUANTUM_BY_SUFFIX has no 1000-quantum case; this file must not be discovered by that enumerator.

bounds_unchanged.note: Both bounds are single-sourced from tests/unit/sparams/test_msl_port_integration.py's MEASURED_SPREAD_ENVELOPE (via tests/_gate_policy.gate_from_envelope) and LEG_S11_BOUND -- this ledger imports them, it does not restate them.

classification_policy.note: POLICY, NOT measured: a same-commit cross-platform spread disagreement >= 0.05 percentage points is classified as platform variance; a shift entering between two same-platform (CI) runs across a commit window is classified as code drift. The measured fact is narrower than this policy number -- no two datums share a commit, so cross-platform agreement is demonstrated as two same-regime PAIRS, not at a fixed commit: pre-drift {dev 0.4607% @69a6956a, GitHub runner 0.46% @90c79d1d, 4 rfx/ commits apart} and post-drift {GitHub runner 0.47% @7f68f9fb and @8e004976, this pod 0.4676% @1f005d0d}. Agreement finer than the 0.01 pp / 0.01 ohm print quantum is NOT MEASURED.

attribution.result: TWO steps, not one. The recipe file itself is byte-identical across the whole window (md5 9faeeba500da9ced30baca8c6d939a04 at 69a6956a, 90c79d1d, 7f68f9fb, 1f005d0d), so the drift is rfx/ code.
attribution.method: per-sha git-archive trees, one process each, driven by that tree's own _run_msl_thru; see the role="bisect" datums below and tests/fixtures/msl_z0_length_invariance/bisect_796.json for the raw per-leg dump.

commits.subject: extend static materials into the CPML pad for domain-face-touching boxes (closes #627)
commits.mechanism: this fixture's substrate Box((0,0,0)-(lx,LY,H_SUB)) is flush with the x-lo/x-hi/y-lo/y-hi domain faces, all CPML. #638 lets a hi-face pad whose naive interior-edge source column reads vacuum source from the column one further in, so the x-hi/y-hi pads went from eps_r=1 to eps_r=EPS_R -- the absorber stops being mismatched against the substrate it terminates.

commits.subject: give the boundary node the material its own pad already gets (closes #655)
commits.mechanism: #638 wrote the recovered material into the pad only, leaving the dropped boundary node vacuum -- a one-cell film between the structure and its own matched absorber. #659 writes the replicated value into the outermost interior column too.

attribution.classification: i -- both are intended absorber-matching corrections with their own measured witnesses (#638: its secondary 'author's independent fixture' witness, edge-touching-slab tail/peak energy -85.15 dB -> -90.62 dB — the PR's headline absorber witness is -95.63 -> -104.25 dB; #659: reflection off the one-cell vacuum film 0.2375 -> exactly 0.0 at the default mesh). Neither is a regression, so the shift is a better-terminated board, not a defect to revert.
attribution.bit_identity_chain: leg-8 mean|Z0[+x]| on the bisect platform: 90c79d1d = ae7919a9 = 57.33811569213867; fce10916 = 5f23ccae = fd37c62f = 57.33358383178711; c9c1864f = 7f68f9fb = 1f005d0d = 57.32954406738281. Legs 10 and 12 follow the same three-value chain.
attribution.corrects: The 2026-09-13 close comment named 7f68f9fb (#666, the x/y axis generalization of add_msl_port) as the only direct MSL-extraction change in the window and closed the issue as superseded by #931. Measurement says #666 moves nothing on this fixture: 7f68f9fb is bit-identical to its parent c9c1864f on all three legs. #645 and #658 (the two dtype lifts) are excluded the same way. The drift sits in #638 and #659.
attribution.gate_disposition: Bisect rows are tagged PASSED so tests/locks/test_msl_z0_platform_datums.py::test_every_passed_datum_is_actually_under_bound checks their recomputation (spread < 0.007, L=12 mean|S11| < 0.15). UNCHANGED and left to the PI. MEASURED_SPREAD_ENVELOPE stays 0.004607 and the enforced gate stays gate_from_envelope(0.004607, quantum=1000) = 0.007. gate_from_envelope(0.004686, quantum=1000) would derive 0.008 -- a ONE-QUANTUM WIDENING, which issue #610's no-silent-loosening rule forbids applying as routine maintenance even when the drift is attributed and benign. Re-deriving the envelope off the post-#638/#659 board is a PI decision, and on current main it would additionally have to be taken on the #931 board, not this one.
attribution.platform_variance_check: this host reads spread 0.4686% at 1f005d0d where the ledger's pod row (jax 0.6.2) reads 0.4676% -- 0.001 pp apart, far inside classification_policy.threshold_pp = 0.05, so the two platforms agree and the steps above are code.
